This is the classic PEP 562 pitfall: when doing `from . import test`, the import system first tries `getattr(py, 'test')` (which recurses) before falling back to the submodule import.

Let me recall: `_handle_fromlist` does: if hasattr(module, x) → skip; else try import module.x. `hasattr(py, 'test')` calls `__getattr__('test')` → recursion.

So the fix: in `__getattr__`, use `importlib.import_module('py.test')` directly, or better: set the attribute in sys.modules first. Standard pattern:

    if name == "test":

        test = importlib.import_module("py.test")

The import system for `import py.test` imports parent `py`, then imports submodule `py.test` via the finder — it does NOT use `__getattr__`. `_handle_fromlist` is what uses hasattr. `importlib.import_module('py.test')` → `_bootstrap._find_and_load('py.test')` — no hasattr on parent. So that works.

Alternatively, simplest: `from . import test as _test` won't help (same _handle_fromlist path). Use importlib.import_module.

If I put the eager `from . import test` at the very END of `__init__.py`, then everything else is defined. pytest importing py mid-init gets a nearly-complete module. Risky but probably fine.
